title: String-based browser timers bypassed dynamic-code execution checks

reproduction.beforeFix: A global setTimeout call with a static source string returned pass. Browser string timers execute source as code even without a direct eval or Function call.
reproduction.afterFix: Static string arguments to global/window setTimeout and setInterval, aliased timer functions, call/apply forms, and Reflect.apply are classified as dynamic code execution. Function callbacks remain allowed.

rootCause: The source gate rejected eval and Function but omitted browser timer APIs that accept source strings as executable code.
remediation: Resolve timer function aliases and reflective references, then reject timer invocations whose first executable argument is statically a string without rejecting ordinary callback functions.

validation.redBeforeFixResult: failed as expected: the global setTimeout source string returned pass
